# Routes

## [v1.9.1](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/tree/v1.9.1) (2026-11-18)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/compare/v1.9.0...v1.9.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/releases)

- Find GatherMate2 node names from its Vanilla locale too  
    On WoW Forever (game types camelot and forever in GatherMate2.toc),  
    GatherMate2 names nodes from its "GatherMate2NodesVanilla" locale,  
    whose names can differ from the "GatherMate2Nodes" ones. In frFR the  
    Vanilla names use a straight apostrophe ("Filon d'étain") and the  
    others a typographic one ("Filon d’étain").  
    AppendNodes only looked in "GatherMate2Nodes", so it returned nil for  
    such a node and the Create Route button failed with "table index is  
    nil" when storing the selection. With Lua errors hidden, nothing  
    happened at all, and a single such node in the selection was enough.  
    When the name is not in "GatherMate2Nodes", look it up in  
    "GatherMate2NodesVanilla" too.  
    In frFR on Forever, 9 nodes failed (Tin, Silver, Gold, Incendicite and  
    Indurium veins, the Ooze Covered Silver and Gold veins, Arthas' Tears  
    and the Stonescale Eel Swarm). deDE, esES and ruRU had the same  
    problem.  
- Add notes for working on the addon  
    How to run the tests, what the clustering and the route optimizer have  
    to guarantee, what their settings are based on, and what is still open.  
    The file is not part of the packaged addon.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add the tests for route clustering and route optimization  
    The tests run in a plain Lua 5.1 interpreter:  
      lua5.1 tests/cluster\_test.lua  
      lua5.1 tests/tsp\_test.lua  
    tests/wow\_shims.lua provides the parts of the WoW API that TSP.lua  
    needs. The data sets in tests/data are generated by cluster\_gen.lua and  
    tsp\_gen.lua, which is deterministic, and contain the results of frozen  
    copies of the original implementations (cluster\_reference.lua and  
    tsp\_reference.lua) to compare with. tsp\_extract.lua turns a route from  
    a saved variables file into test cases, one real route is included.  
    The tests folder is not part of the packaged addon.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Fix some variable shadowing and other minor mistakes

## [v1.9.0](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/tree/v1.9.0) (2026-11-12)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/compare/v1.8.7...v1.9.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/releases)

- Ignore local testing harness  
- Let the background route optimization try for longer before giving up  
    It gave up after 5 attempts per node without an improvement, which is  
    half of what the foreground optimization always tries, so optimizing  
    again in the foreground often still improved a route that the  
    background optimization had given up on. On a real route improvements  
    were up to 20 attempts per node apart.  
    Give up after 30 attempts per node without an improvement instead, and  
    raise the limit to 300 attempts per node.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Swap longer segments when kicking the route  
    Swapping segments of up to 100 instead of up to 30 nodes takes about  
    two thirds longer per kick, but found shorter routes in the same time  
    on all routes it was compared on, including a real route of 475  
    clusters and its 2037 nodes: those were 0.4% and 1.3% shorter after 10  
    kicks per node, more than 10 times as many of the shorter kicks got.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Calculate fewer distances in the route optimizer  
    Keep the cost of travelling to each neighbour of a node next to the  
    list of its neighbours instead of calculating it again every time, and  
    calculate the cost of the 2 links of a node only once for all the moves  
    that are tried for that node. The segment of just that one node was  
    also looked at twice.  
    This makes no difference for the routes that are found, but takes about  
    a third less time.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Don't optimize a route in the foreground while it is optimized in the background  
    The foreground result replaced the route, after which the stop button  
    did not recognize the background run anymore, and the result of the  
    background run replaced the route again when it finished.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Make the route optimizer robust against lopsided routes and touching taboos  
    Finding the neighbours of the nodes took quadratic time if most nodes  
    ended up in a few cells of the grid, which is sized by the bounding box  
    of the route: for example with one node far away from all the others,  
    or with many nodes on the same spot. The cells are now made smaller  
    until no cell has too many nodes, a node that is far away from all  
    others looks at all nodes instead of walking through empty cells, and  
    nodes on the same spot stop looking after a while.  
    Whether a line crosses a taboo region could depend on the order of its  
    2 nodes if it merely touched the outline. As the answers are cached and  
    the cache is emptied when it gets too big, the same line could be rated  
    differently later on, and the cost of the route that is kept track of  
    was off by a whole taboo penalty. Always ask in the same order.  
    Also finish a stopped background run during the first pass already, and  
    don't let the progress that is reported go backwards.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Remove the extra optimization option  
    With the new route optimizer nearly all of the improvement is found  
    early on. Trying 5 times as long made the test routes at most 0.5%  
    shorter, which is not worth an option.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Remove the 724 node limit of the route optimizer and add a stop button  
    The new route optimizer has no NxN matrix anymore, so there is no need  
    to limit the size of a route.  
    The background optimization now keeps trying to improve the route until  
    it had no success for a while, and can be stopped with the new stop  
    button, keeping the best route found so far. The "Extra optimization"  
    option now makes both the foreground and the background optimization  
    try 5 times as long.  
    The settings of the ant colony optimization are gone, and the help  
    texts describe the new algorithm.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add an effort setting and a way to stop the background route optimizer  
    SolveTSP() now takes the number of attempts to improve the route per  
    node, and optionally the number of attempts without an improvement  
    after which it gives up early. StopTSP() makes a background run finish  
    with the best route it has found so far.  
    Also return the error message instead of the path argument when  
    starting the background optimization fails, and reset the state of the  
    background optimization before calling the finish function.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Kick the route out of local optimums and add neighbours in all directions  
    Once no single move improves the route anymore, swap 2 short segments  
    of the route that are next to each other, improve the route again  
    around them, and undo all of that if the route did not get shorter. All  
    changes to the route are reversals of a part of it, so undoing is just  
    doing them again backwards.  
    The neighbours of a node now include the 2 nearest nodes in each of the  
    4 directions. In a dense group of nodes, the nearest neighbours of a  
    node used to be all from its own group, so better links to other groups  
    were never tried.  
    With 10 neighbours and 10 kicks per node the routes are 1.4% to 5.8%  
    shorter than those of the ant colony optimization on the test routes,  
    724 nodes take 1.2 seconds instead of 28.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Replace the ant colony route optimizer with a local search  
    The ant colony optimization kept 3 NxN matrices, which limited routes  
    to 724 nodes, and spent most of its time in a 2-opt pass that looked at  
    a large part of all node pairs: optimizing 724 nodes took about half a  
    minute.  
    The new solver improves a greedy route (or the given route, if that is  
    shorter) with 2-opt and Or-opt moves that are only tried between a node  
    and its 8 nearest neighbours, which are found with a grid. Distances  
    are calculated when needed instead of being kept in a matrix, so time  
    and memory are roughly proportional to the number of nodes. 20000 nodes  
    take less than half a second.  
    Lines crossing a taboo region are still penalized the same way, but the  
    check now also works for vertical lines. In the background mode, the  
    setup is now done in time slices too and the route is read before  
    yielding for the first time.  
    On its own this finds routes that are between 3% shorter and 11% longer  
    than before, the next step makes up for that.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Limit the size of the clustering grid  
    With an absurdly large zone or a tiny cluster radius the cell keys of  
    the grid were too large to be exact integers, which made the loops over  
    the neighbouring cells never end.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Fix two races in background route clustering  
    The route was only read on the first frame after the clustering was  
    started, while its size was taken at the start. Removing a node from  
    the route in between made the clustering fail with an error. Read the  
    route before yielding for the first time.  
    Starting a background optimization on a route that was being clustered  
    in the background silently reverted the clustering once the  
    optimization finished. Don't allow optimizing such a route.  
    Co-Auth

## [v1.8.7](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/tree/v1.8.7) (2026-05-13)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/compare/v1.8.6...v1.8.7) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Nevcairiel/Routes/releases)

- Update TOC  
- Fix zone name collision causing data loss for identically-named zones  
    When two zones share the same localized name (e.g. Zul'Aman outdoor zone  
    and Zul'Aman dungeon instance), processMapEntries() would silently  
    overwrite Routes.LZName[name] with whichever mapID happened to be  
    iterated last by pairs(). The losing mapID's routes became unreachable  
    and plugins (GatherMate2 etc.) inserting nodes would store them under  
    the wrong mapID via the same lookup.  
    Replace the single-pass loop with a two-pass approach:  
    - Pass 1 collects all name→[id…] mappings.  
    - Collision phase builds a disambiguatedZoneNames cache keyed by uiMapID,  
      using the parent zone's localized name as the suffix (matching the  
      existing pattern for Dalaran, Shadowmoon Valley, etc.), with a numeric  
      fallback when parent names are absent or also collide.  
    - Pass 2 populates LZName using the final, unique names.  
    GetZoneName() is updated to check disambiguatedZoneNames first so that  
    Routes.GetZoneName(id) — called by plugins to convert a mapID to a name  
    before passing it to InsertNode/DeleteNode — returns the same unique  
    string that was stored in LZName.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Update interface version in Routes.toc  
    Bump TOC to 120000 on confirmation in issue #42
